summary: Intermittent 403s on presigned S3 artifact downloads caused by TLS session pool sharing at customer egress proxy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403 Forbidden errors when Redwood Private serving nodes attempt to download model artifacts via presigned S3 URLs. Failures are sporadic (roughly 1 in 20 attempts) and impact model startup on a subset of serving nodes.

Impact: Several model pulls during scale-ups fail leading to increased cold-start latencies and transient 5xx errors observed by customer application. Customer has dedicated Private deployment in us-west-2 and is on a timetable for a feature launch.

Environment: Private deploy behind customer-managed egress proxy (corporate forward proxy) that performs TLS session pooling/offloading for outbound HTTPS connections. Serving nodes run on k8s nodes in the customer's VPC with normal egress via the proxy path.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger serving node scale-up to pull artifact: kubectl scale deployment model-worker --replicas=10
2) Observe artifact download attempts in worker logs (artifact fetcher uses presigned S3 URL returned by control plane)
3) Some workers report HTTP 403 on GET to presigned URL; retry succeeds for same URL in many cases
4) Reproduce is more likely under concurrency (20+ parallel pulls) and when proxy TLS session pool is active
logs:
[2026-03-10T09:12:15Z] artifact-fetcher INFO downloading https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/acme-models/prefix/model.tar.gz?X-Amz-Signature=...
[2026-03-10T09:12:15Z] artifact-fetcher ERROR http status=403 content="AccessDenied: SignatureDoesNotMatch" attempt=1
[2026-03-10T09:12:16Z] artifact-fetcher INFO retrying download (attempt=2)
[2026-03-10T09:12:16Z] artifact-fetcher INFO download succeeded

Proxy tcpdump excerpt (customer supplied):
  client-src=10.10.5.12:45678 -> proxy:443  TLSv1.2 Handshake (SNI: s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com)
  client-src=10.10.5.13:56789 -> proxy:443  TLS session reused (no SNI) -> backend connection reused to s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: presigned URL signature mismatch indicates Host header / TLS SNI seen by S3 did not match the host used when signing or when creating the canonical request. Collected packet capture from customer egress proxy and compared TLS server_name indications to the Host header in proxied requests.

Findings:
- The customer egress proxy performs TLS session pooling and will resume sessions across connections regardless of the requested SNI if the backend certificate is valid.
- In pooled/resumed sessions the proxy sometimes forwards requests on a backend connection that was originally established to a different virtual host, causing mismatch between TLS server_name and Host header seen by AWS S3.
- AWS S3 validates the presigned URL signature against expected host/canonical request; when SNI/host mismatch occurs S3 responds with SignatureDoesNotMatch -> 403.
- Replays show retries often succeed because a new non-pooled connection is created or the session used happens to match the expected SNI.

Reproduction done with cURL through customer's proxy under high concurrency mirrored the behavior (enabled with --verbose and reuse enabled in the proxy).
comments: 2026-03-10 13:22 - Maya Singh (Support): Initial customer report received; requested packet capture and proxy config details. Customer provided proxy vendor (BlueWave Proxy) and config snippet showing TLS session reuse = enabled.

2026-03-10 16:08 - Evan Patel (SRE): Confirmed 403s correlate with proxy connection reuse. Attachments: pcap excerpt, worker logs. Asked customer to run a controlled test disabling session reuse for s3 hostnames.

2026-03-11 09:37 - Acme Eng (customer): Disabled session pooling for domains matching '*.s3.amazonaws.com' as a test. Error rate dropped to ~0.1% from ~5% during concurrent pulls. Customer will test for 24 hours.

2026-03-11 18:05 - Evan Patel (SRE): Suggested long-term fixes: (1) configure proxy to preserve SNI and avoid reusing backend TLS sessions across different hostnames; (2) pin S3 egress to a dedicated NAT without proxy; (3) update artifact fetcher to retry with new connection on SignatureDoesNotMatch (short-term). Logged follow-up task INT-44512 to track artifact-fetcher retry hardening.
2026-03-12 08:12 - Maya Singh (Support): Customer confirmed workaround in place; monitoring continues. Preparing postmortem template and suggested doc for private deploy runbook.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied by customer: disabled TLS session pooling for S3 hostname patterns on their corporate proxy and configured a bypass rule for artifact fetch traffic. Immediate impact: 95% reduction in presigned URL 403s during concurrent pulls.

Planned next steps:
- Customer: keep bypass for S3 for 7 days and report any regressions.
- Redwood: add a short-term artifact-fetcher mitigation to force new TLS connections when SignatureDoesNotMatch on presigned URLs (tracked in INT-44512).
- Joint: create guidance in private deployment runbook describing proxy configuration recommendations (preserve SNI, avoid cross-host session reuse, or whitelist S3 endpoints).

Root cause: customer egress proxy TLS session pool reused backend TLS sessions across different hostnames, leading to mismatched TLS SNI vs HTTP Host for presigned S3 requests which in turn produced SignatureDoesNotMatch / 403 responses from S3.

Status: Waiting on customer validation window (24-72h). Once stable we will move ticket to Resolved and record runbook addition.
next_steps: Customer to monitor for 72h and confirm stable (point-of-contact: Acme Eng)
Redwood to backport retry-hardening to artifact-fetcher (INT-44512)
Support to draft runbook section on egress proxy config for presigned URL traffic
